handbookNote: West Virginia Commercial Driver's License Manual (WV DMV-specific front matter Rev. 08/2023, layered onto the AAMVA-authored '2005 CDL Testing System' base manual, Version: July 2017 -- same AAMVA base-manual generation used by several other CDL-track states in this project, e.g. Louisiana and Rhode Island), published by the West Virginia Department of Transportation, Division of Motor Vehicles (WV DMV) -- fetched directly from https://webapps.transportation.wv.gov/TWS/WVDOTDocumentStorageMigration/PDF/Transportation/DMV/DMVFormSearch/WV-CDL-Manual.pdf on 2026-08-24 (the transportation.wv.gov-hosted convenience URL, https://transportation.wv.gov/DMV/DMVFormSearch/WV-CDL-Manual.pdf, returned a 404 'site under construction/migrating documents' page at fetch time; the working URL above was located via the official WV DMV 'Driver's Licensing Handbooks' page at dmv.wv.gov/driver-services/drivers/drivers-licensing-handbooks, which links it as 'Download the Commercial Driver License (CDL) Manual' -- both are official WV.gov government sources, and the working link is a WV DOT-operated document-storage-migration host, not a third party) -- 7.96MB PDF, full text extracted via pdftotext -layout to scratchpad/wv_cdl_research/wv_cdl_manual_full.txt, 11,526 lines. Price matches this project's established CDL tier ($6.99). Real exam mechanics: the WV-specific front matter's own 'Knowledge Test' section states explicitly and unambiguously 'The knowledge test must be taken and passed, with at least an 80% score' (matching the federally standardized 80% minimum under 49 CFR 383.135(a), applied identically across every CDL-track state in this project) -- this passing-score figure IS confirmed directly from an official WV.gov source and is asserted as fact. However, NEITHER the WV-specific front matter NOR the AAMVA base-manual text anywhere states an exact knowledge-test item count (e.g. a '50 questions' or '25 questions' figure) for the general knowledge test or any endorsement test -- the manual's own CDL Fee Chart merely says knowledge testing buys 'three (3) attempts' per $32.50 fee and that a failed test requires a seven (7) day wait before retesting, without ever stating how many questions make up an attempt. Per this project's no-default-values discipline, this item-count figure is explicitly hedged rather than assumed, invented, or borrowed from another state's manual or from this project's own CA/TX/NY/etc. 50-question default -- consistent with how Louisiana, Montana, and New Mexico's tracks in this project were built when their own official manuals were equally silent on the exact number. What IS additionally confirmed directly from official WV sources: WV's CDL classes A/B/C/D per the WV-specific front matter (Class D being WV's own non-commercial-vehicles-for-hire category, distinct from the AAMVA base manual's three-class A/B/C federal framework); six CDL endorsement codes H (Hazardous Materials, TSA fingerprint/background check required), N (Tank Vehicles), P (Passengers, skills test required), T (Doubles/Triples), S (School Bus, skills test required), and X (combined Hazmat + Tank, TSA check required) -- WV's front matter separately lists an 'F' Motorcycle endorsement, but this is a general driver's-license endorsement, not one of the six CDL-specific knowledge-test endorsements, a distinction preserved rather than conflated; ten WV-specific restriction codes E, K, L, M, N, O, P, V, X, Z (WV's own wording for several of these, e.g. M = 'restricts driver to class B or C buses only' and N = 'restricts driver to buses 26,000 pounds and under (Class C buses)', differs in phrasing/scope from other states' restriction tables and was preserved as WV states it, not harmonized to another state's wording); a WV Commercial Learner's Permit (CLP) is valid 180 days, renewable once within 2 years of initial issuance, and must be held a minimum of 14 days before the skills test may be taken; the CDL skills test costs $100 (a $50 no-show fee applies) and is administered only by certified third-party examiners, never by the state directly; HAZMAT/X endorsement applicants must complete a TSA fingerprint-based background check via Universal Enrollment Services (UES, $86.50 fee) before testing; CDL expiration follows a birthday-based 3-to-8-year cycle tied to age-divisible-by-5 rules for holders 21 and older; a CDL more than six months expired requires retaking both Class E (WV's non-commercial license class) and CDL knowledge/skills tests. Content-depth rationale: WV's manual is organized into the same 13 AAMVA core sections used by other same-generation CDL-track states in this project -- Section 1 Introduction (combined with the WV-specific front matter's definitions/licensing/fees/endorsements/restrictions/disqualifications into the licensing bucket), Section 2 Driving Safely (the largest section by far, split into two buckets: 02_driving_safely_a covering subsections 2.1 Vehicle Inspection through 2.16 Mountain Driving, 03_driving_safely_b covering 2.17 Driving Emergencies through the hazardous-materials-rules-for-all-drivers close of Section 2), Section 3 Transporting Cargo Safely, Section 4 Transporting Passengers Safely, Section 5 Air Brakes, Section 6 Combination Vehicles, Section 7 Doubles and Triples, Section 8 Tank Vehicles (the shortest section in this manual, only about 2 pages), Section 9 Hazardous Materials (the second-largest section, split into two buckets: 10_hazmat_a covering subsections 9.1 Intent of the Regulations through 9.4 Loading and Unloading, 11_hazmat_b covering 9.5 Bulk Packaging Marking/Loading through the 9.8 Hazardous Materials Glossary), Section 10 School Buses, Section 11 Vehicle Inspection, and Section 12 Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test combined with Section 13 On-Road Driving into one closing bucket -- the same 14-bucket structure used by Rhode Island's track in this project. Sections naturally short in this manual (Cargo: 24 questions, Passenger: 26, Doubles/Triples: 24, Tank Vehicles: 18 -- the smallest bucket in the track, matching its ~2-page source depth) were sized down accordingly rather than padded to match larger sections; Driving Safely (120 questions across two buckets), Hazardous Materials (95 questions across two buckets), Air Brakes (60), School Bus (59), Combination Vehicles (56), and Vehicle Inspection (44) supported deeper coverage and were sized up accordingly, reflecting genuine manual depth rather than an artificial per-bucket target. Every question in this bank is grounded in a specific passage of the fetched official West Virginia manual text cited in that question's source_note; none are invented, generic, or borrowed from another state's numbers -- all numeric specifications (tank gallon thresholds, air brake PSI ranges, endorsement fees, CLP validity periods, restriction-code definitions, school-bus danger-zone/tail-swing figures, hazmat placard/parking-distance thresholds) were verified against the actual West Virginia text read during drafting, independently re-verified by the top-level agent afterward via a structural/field-integrity script run across all 14 bucket files (0 malformed rows, 0 exact-duplicate questions across 586 raw questions) plus direct spot-reads of sampled questions against the underlying manual text, and via a direct correct_choice letter-distribution tally per bucket file (every bucket's per-letter share fell between 20% and 31%, well inside the 15-35% project target -- no bucket required post-hoc rebalancing by the top-level agent, though several drafting sub-agents self-corrected their own initial skew, e.g. School Bus, before reporting completion). Several bucket-drafting sub-agents ran unusually long or produced duplicate/conflicting attempts on the same output file mid-build (a recurring risk in this pipeline); every file's actual on-disk content was re-verified by the top-level agent only after confirming stability across repeated checks, not from any sub-agent's self-report.
